proposal.hypothesis: The current random forest is trained on only 300 samples per basin, which may undersample rarer hydrological regimes (e.g., snowmelt or storm peaks) within each catchment, limiting the model's ability to generalize across the full seasonal cycle captured in development validation.
proposal.expected_effect: Increasing per-basin training samples should improve median KGE and log-NSE by giving the forest denser coverage of each catchment's flow regime, while keeping max_depth and min_samples_leaf unchanged to avoid added overfitting risk.

proposal.hypothesis: Bootstrapping only 75% of samples per tree may systematically undersample rare high-flow events within each basin's training pool, producing the persistent 7-10% median absolute PBIAS seen across recent random_forest trials; increasing the bootstrap fraction toward the full sample gives each tree more consistent exposure to peak-flow observations.
proposal.expected_effect: median_abs_pbias should decrease as trees see a more representative sample of high-flow events per basin, with median_kge stable or slightly improved from reduced volume bias; minor risk of reduced tree diversity is offset by unchanged n_estimators.

proposal.hypothesis: At max_depth=18 the forest may be underfitting complex nonlinear interactions between static catchment attributes (topography, soil, geology) and dynamic drivers across the 100 diverse development catchments, producing the persistent 7-9% median absolute PBIAS seen across recent trials regardless of sampling strategy; allowing deeper trees should let the model better separate catchment-specific regimes.
proposal.expected_effect: Deeper trees should better capture catchment-specific nonlinear interactions, reducing median absolute PBIAS and improving median KGE, while min_samples_leaf=4 continues to guard against leaf-level overfitting.

proposal.hypothesis: The current min_samples_leaf=4 forces excessive averaging within terminal nodes, smoothing out peak-flow observations and driving the persistent 7-9% median absolute PBIAS seen across recent trials, independent of sample size or tree depth adjustments already tested.
proposal.expected_effect: Finer leaf resolution should let trees better isolate high-flow observations, reducing median absolute PBIAS while KGE and log-NSE remain stable or improve since bagging over 200 estimators still controls variance.

proposal.hypothesis: Rolling windows of 180 and 365 days exceed the random forest's max_dynamic_window=90 cap, so those long-window features are structurally unusable by the trees yet still dilute the feature space and correlate with the shorter windows, weakening split quality and likely contributing to the persistent ~7-9% median absolute PBIAS seen across four consecutive hyperparameter-only mutations (sample size, max_samples, max_depth, min_samples_leaf) that failed to move the bias.
proposal.expected_effect: Trimming the feature set to only windows within the model's effective 90-day horizon should reduce collinearity/noise at split selection, improving median_kge and log_nse and reducing median_abs_pbias by sharpening the signal used for peak- and low-flow partitioning.

proposal.hypothesis: Rolling windows of 180 and 365 days exceed the random forest's fixed max_dynamic_window=90 cap, so those long-window features are never actually usable by trees yet still add multicollinear noise to the candidate split pool, likely degrading split quality relative to the 62.77-scoring baseline.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing structurally unusable long-window features should sharpen split selection on the effective 1-90 day windows, improving median_kge and log_nse stability and reducing the persistent ~7% median absolute PBIAS caused by diluted feature importance.

proposal.hypothesis: Six consecutive single-parameter mutations to max_depth, min_samples_leaf, max_samples, and sample_per_basin_train all underperformed the 62.77 baseline, suggesting the persistent 7-9% PBIAS and KGE variance are driven by ensemble noise rather than per-tree capacity or sampling depth, so increasing the number of trees (untested in this decision space) should reduce prediction variance and stabilize peak-flow estimates without further overfitting.
proposal.expected_effect: median_kge and composite_score should improve via reduced ensemble variance and more stable out-of-bag averaging, while median_abs_pbias should remain roughly unchanged since more trees do not alter the model's systematic bias structure.

proposal.hypothesis: Seven consecutive single-parameter mutations to depth, leaf size, sample fraction, and window pruning all failed to reach the 62.77 baseline, suggesting ensemble prediction variance from only 200 trees (rather than per-tree capacity or sampling) is the limiting factor for both KGE and PBIAS stability.
proposal.expected_effect: Doubling the ensemble size should reduce prediction variance across trees, stabilizing median KGE and log-NSE and reducing the spread in median absolute PBIAS relative to the 200-tree baseline.

proposal.hypothesis: Eight consecutive hyperparameter-only mutations (sample size, max_samples, depth, leaf size, window pruning, n_estimators) all underperformed the 62.77 baseline, suggesting the bottleneck is feature redundancy rather than tree capacity, and the three highly correlated temperature variables (mean/max/min) may be diluting split quality by competing for the same information.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the redundant 2m_temp_max and 2m_temp_min features should reduce multicollinearity among candidate splits, letting trees select more discriminative variables and improving median KGE while stabilizing median absolute PBIAS.

proposal.hypothesis: Nine consecutive mutations increasing model flexibility (deeper trees, larger bootstrap fraction, more trees, finer leaves) all failed to beat baseline while median_abs_pbias stayed pinned at 7-9%, suggesting the forest is overfitting to basin-specific training peaks rather than underfitting; pulling max_depth down from 18 toward a shallower, more regularized tree should reduce variance-driven bias and improve generalization to development-validation flows.
proposal.expected_effect: Shallower trees should reduce overfitting to per-basin training peaks, lowering median_abs_pbias and stabilizing median_kge/median_log_nse relative to the last nine rejected trials.

proposal.hypothesis: Both directions of tree-capacity tuning (deeper in i03, shallower in i10) and both directions of bootstrap fraction (i02 increased) have failed to beat the 62.77 baseline while depth=18 and leaf=4 sit at a local optimum, so an untested lever is reducing max_samples below the current 0.75 to increase inter-tree decorrelation and shrink the ensemble variance that drives the persistent PBIAS/KGE instability, independent of per-tree complexity.
proposal.expected_effect: Lower per-tree bootstrap fraction should decorrelate trees and reduce ensemble prediction variance, tightening median_kge and stabilizing median_abs_pbias without reintroducing the bias-variance regressions seen when depth or leaf size were altered.

proposal.hypothesis: Eleven consecutive single-hyperparameter mutations (depth up/down, leaf size, max_samples up/down, n_estimators up, sample_per_basin_train up, window pruning) all underperformed the 62.77 baseline, confirming the current n_estimators=200/max_depth=18/min_samples_leaf=4/max_samples=0.75 point is a local optimum in hyperparameter space, so the remaining lever is feature composition: surface pressure has weak direct physical coupling to runoff generation compared to precipitation, temperature, SWE, ET, and soil moisture, and likely dilutes split quality by competing with more informative predictors across 100 heterogeneous catchments.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the low-signal surf_press predictor should reduce split competition from noise, improving split quality on high-value predictors and modestly raising median_kge and median_log_nse while stabilizing median_abs_pbias relative to the 7% plateau seen across all recent hyperparameter-only trials.

proposal.hypothesis: Twelve consecutive hyperparameter-only mutations across tree capacity, sampling, and bootstrap fraction all failed to beat the 62.77 baseline, pointing to feature redundancy rather than model capacity as the limiting factor, and surface pressure has weak direct physical influence on catchment runoff generation compared to precipitation, snowmelt, ET, and soil moisture, so it likely adds low-signal noise that dilutes split quality in the random forest.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the low-signal surface pressure predictor should improve split quality on the remaining hydrologically informative features, reducing median_abs_pbias and improving median_kge relative to the 62.77 baseline.

proposal.hypothesis: Depth-based regularisation (i10) caused sharp degradation by globally truncating tree structure, but leaf-size regularisation acts more locally on terminal-node homogeneity and has only been probed in the decreasing direction (i04); increasing min_samples_leaf from 4 to 6 should curb noisy peak-flow leaf estimates without the catastrophic underfitting seen when depth was cut.
proposal.expected_effect: Median absolute PBIAS should drop below the persistent 7% floor as leaf averaging stabilises peak-flow predictions, while median KGE should hold near or above 0.61 since the effect is more localized than the harmful depth reduction in i10.

proposal.hypothesis: Snow water equivalent is near-zero across a large share of the 100 development catchments (many lowland/non-alpine basins), so keeping it as a predictor consumes split capacity on a mostly-sparse, low-variance signal and dilutes tree quality in the same way the tested temperature/pressure redundancy did, without providing runoff-relevant information for most basins.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the sparse, mostly-uninformative swe predictor should sharpen split quality on the remaining precipitation/temperature/soil-moisture features, reducing the persistent 7-9% median absolute PBIAS and nudging median KGE and composite_score back toward the 62.77 baseline.

proposal.hypothesis: The i10 result showed that increasing model flexibility (deeper trees, more bootstrap data, more trees) sharply worsened PBIAS, indicating the forest overfits to basin-specific training peaks; reducing sample_per_basin_train (only tested upward in i08) should shrink this overfitting by limiting how many redundant peak-flow observations per basin the trees can memorize, without the catastrophic capacity loss caused by truncating max_depth.
proposal.expected_effect: Lower per-basin sample density should reduce variance-driven overfitting to basin-specific peaks, tightening median_abs_pbias and improving median_kge/log_nse stability relative to the 62.77 baseline.

proposal.hypothesis: The i09 hypothesis that redundant, highly-correlated temperature variables (2m_temp_max, 2m_temp_min duplicating 2m_temp_mean) dilute split quality was proposed but never actually executed as a mutation in subsequent iterations, which instead tested capacity/sampling levers exclusively, so this remains the one untested feature-composition lever from the approved list.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the two collinear temperature duplicates should free split capacity for genuinely independent predictors (precipitation, ET, soil moisture), improving median KGE/log-NSE and reducing the persistent 7-9% median absolute PBIAS caused by noisy competing splits.

proposal.hypothesis: The three temperature variables (2m_temp_mean, 2m_temp_max, 2m_temp_min) are highly collinear, so retaining all three lets redundant near-duplicate features compete for splits and dilutes the effective information density of the candidate pool at each node, an untested feature-composition lever distinct from the window-pruning and SWE-removal tests already rejected.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing 2m_temp_max and 2m_temp_min should sharpen split quality by freeing candidate-feature slots for less redundant predictors, improving median_kge and reducing median_abs_pbias relative to the 62.77 baseline without changing any hyperparameters already shown to sit at a local optimum.

proposal.hypothesis: The i09/i17/i18 iterations repeatedly identified that 2m_temp_max and 2m_temp_min are near-duplicates of 2m_temp_mean and dilute split quality, but this feature-composition mutation was never actually executed (those three iterations show identical scorecards to each other), so removing the two redundant temperature features while retaining 2m_temp_mean is still the one genuinely untested lever after twelve capacity/sampling mutations failed.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the two collinear temperature duplicates should free split capacity at each node for genuinely informative predictors (precipitation, soil moisture, ET), reducing noisy peak-flow leaf estimates and improving both median_kge and median_abs_pbias relative to the 62.77 baseline.

proposal.hypothesis: 2m_temp_max and 2m_temp_min are near-duplicates of 2m_temp_mean (all three derive from the same diurnal temperature signal), so retaining all three lets redundant collinear features compete for splits at each node and dilutes the effective information density of the random subset of candidate features, an untested feature-composition lever after twelve consecutive hyperparameter-only mutations failed to beat the 62.77 baseline.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the two redundant temperature duplicates should sharpen split selection on the remaining informative predictors, improving median_kge and median_log_nse and reducing median_abs_pbias by letting trees allocate splits to genuinely distinct signals (precipitation, snowmelt, ET, soil moisture, radiation, pressure) instead of three collinear temperature variants.

proposal.hypothesis: 2m_temp_max and 2m_temp_min are near-duplicates of 2m_temp_mean, so dropping them frees split capacity for less collinear predictors without losing the diurnal temperature signal that 2m_temp_mean already carries.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the two redundant temperature features should raise median_kge and median_log_nse by improving split quality per tree, while leaving median_abs_pbias roughly unchanged since no capacity/sampling parameters are touched.

proposal.hypothesis: Twelve iterations of hyperparameter tuning and the previously-repeated (but never actually executed, since 2m_temp_max/min are already absent from the feature list) temperature-redundancy mutation have all failed to beat baseline, so the genuinely untested feature-composition lever is net thermal radiation, which is more weakly and indirectly linked to runoff generation than net solar radiation (already retained, drives ET/snowmelt) and likely adds collinear, low-signal splits similar to the already-rejected surface-pressure removal.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the redundant, weak-signal thermal radiation feature should free split capacity for stronger runoff predictors, modestly improving median_kge and median_log_nse while leaving median_abs_pbias roughly unchanged since this targets split quality rather than peak-flow bias.

proposal.hypothesis: The i16 reduction of sample_per_basin_train produced the second-best result among all rejected mutations (composite 54.35 vs 51-54 for hyperparameter-only tweaks), suggesting fewer duplicated per-basin training samples curbs the peak-flow overfitting that drives PBIAS instability, so pushing sample_per_basin_train further down toward the range floor should continue that beneficial trend rather than reversing it.
proposal.expected_effect: Further reduction in redundant per-basin peak-flow duplication should lower median PBIAS and stabilize median KGE/log-NSE relative to the i16 result, continuing the only directional lever tested so far that improved on the local hyperparameter optimum.

proposal.hypothesis: Reducing sample_per_basin_train from 150 toward the range floor (100) should further curb the peak-flow overfitting that drives PBIAS instability, extending the direction that produced the best composite score (54.35) among all rejected mutations in i16, as explicitly recommended by the i03 follow-up analysis.
proposal.expected_effect: median_abs_pbias should decrease toward or below the 7.11 baseline by limiting duplicated high-flow observations per basin, with median_kge and median_log_nse stabilizing or improving as trees rely less on memorized basin-specific peaks.

proposal.hypothesis: In i10 the combined increase of depth+samples+trees caused catastrophic PBIAS degradation, but that confounded three factors at once; raising n_estimators alone (more trees, same depth/leaf constraints) should reduce ensemble variance through additional averaging rather than increasing any single tree's capacity to overfit basin-specific peaks, an isolated lever never tested by itself in this run.
proposal.expected_effect: median_kge and median_log_nse should improve modestly via variance reduction from more independent trees, while median_abs_pbias should stay near baseline (not spike like the i10 combined-capacity mutation) since tree depth and leaf size remain unchanged.

proposal.hypothesis: Bootstrap subsample fraction (max_samples) has never been mutated despite being a direct lever on tree-to-tree correlation, and since every capacity-increasing change (deeper trees, more samples, more trees) worsened PBIAS while capacity-reducing changes only helped modestly, shrinking the per-tree bootstrap fraction from 0.75 toward 0.6 should decorrelate trees and dampen ensemble sensitivity to basin-specific peak-flow outliers without discarding any feature information.
proposal.expected_effect: Lower max_samples should reduce correlation among trees' bootstrap draws, curbing the peak-flow overfitting that drives median_abs_pbias up, while median_kge and median_log_nse should hold roughly steady since overall information content per feature is unchanged.

proposal.hypothesis: Every capacity-increasing lever tested (deeper trees, more bootstrap samples, more estimators combined in i10) sharply worsened PBIAS through basin-specific peak overfitting, yet max_depth itself has never been reduced in isolation, so pruning tree depth directly from 18 toward 12 should curb overfitting to per-basin peak flows and stabilise PBIAS without the confounding of the earlier multi-factor capacity increase.
proposal.expected_effect: median_abs_pbias should drop toward or below the ~6.8 baseline range by limiting tree-level memorisation of basin-specific peak events, with composite_score improving via reduced PBIAS variance even if median_kge shifts only marginally.

proposal.hypothesis: Every capacity-increasing lever (deeper trees, larger bootstrap fraction, more estimators) has worsened PBIAS through basin-specific peak memorization, yet min_samples_leaf—the most direct per-leaf regularization control—has never been mutated in isolation from its current value of 4, so raising it should force each leaf to average over more samples and curb overfitting to per-basin peak flows.
proposal.expected_effect: Median PBIAS should improve (shrink toward zero) as larger leaves smooth predictions and reduce basin-specific peak-flow memorization, with KGE/log-NSE held roughly stable since this is a direct regularization lever rather than a capacity or sampling change.

proposal.hypothesis: The dynamic feature set already excludes the collinear temperature duplicates and the extreme thermal-radiation variable (both of the last five 'reject' iterations mutated a no-op, since 2m_temp_max/min/surf_net_therm_rad_mean are not in the current list), so the untested principal-factor lever remaining in the approved space is the antecedent-window depth: retaining 180- and 365-day rolling windows across all 8 dynamic variables inflates the per-split candidate feature pool with long-tail, low-marginal-information features for these meso-scale catchments, diluting split quality the same way excess sample duplication did in i03.
proposal.expected_effect: Trimming the two longest, least-informative antecedent windows should reduce noisy/redundant feature competition at each split, stabilising median PBIAS and modestly improving median KGE/log-NSE similarly to the moderate sample-reduction gain seen in i03, without losing the seasonal memory already captured by the retained 90-day window.

proposal.hypothesis: All prior 'temperature redundancy' iterations (i18-i20, i01) mistakenly proposed removing 2m_temp_max/2m_temp_min, which were never in the active feature set (confirmed as no-ops in i02), so the genuinely untested lever is actually adding 2m_temp_max: daily maximum temperature drives peak daytime snowmelt and evapotranspiration demand distinctly from the diurnal mean, information the current mean-only temperature signal cannot capture even though the two are correlated.
proposal.expected_effect: Adding the maximum-temperature signal should sharpen the model's representation of peak melt/ET-driven flow timing, improving median KGE and reducing PBIAS on peak events without the dilution risk of including all three temperature variants at once.

proposal.hypothesis: The 365-day antecedent window is the longest and most redundant with static catchment attributes (climate normals, geology, soil), contributing stale/noisy information at each split, whereas the 180-day window still encodes within-year seasonal soil-moisture and snowmelt memory that is directly relevant to runoff generation; i09 tested removing both 180 and 365 together (composite 56.62, the joint-best reject) but conflated the two, so isolating removal of only the noisier 365-day window while retaining the informative 180-day window is the untested refinement.
proposal.expected_effect: Median KGE and log-NSE should improve modestly as splits are freed from the least informative, most redundant long-lag aggregate, while PBIAS should remain stable or improve slightly since the 180-day seasonal soil-moisture signal that anchors baseflow/peak timing is preserved, unlike the fully-stripped i09 variant.

proposal.hypothesis: The RF model's max_dynamic_window=90 caps it from ever using the 180/365-day rolling windows (explaining why the last several window-removal iterations were no-ops with identical scores), but the 60-day window IS within that effective range and sits adjacent to both the 30-day and 90-day windows, so it largely duplicates their antecedent soil-moisture/precipitation memory and dilutes split quality at each node; removing it targets a genuinely active redundancy rather than the inert long windows tested previously.
proposal.expected_effect: Median KGE and log-NSE should improve modestly as trees select from less collinear antecedent windows within the effective 0-90 day range, with PBIAS roughly unchanged since no capacity or sampling parameters are touched.

proposal.hypothesis: Both real (non-no-op) tests of sample_per_basin_train moved downward from 150 toward the range floor (i04) and made PBIAS/overfitting worse, implying the current value already errs on the side of too little per-basin sample diversity; moving in the untested upward direction should give each tree more varied basin examples and reduce variance without touching tree capacity (depth/leaf/estimators), which is the axis that has repeatedly hurt PBIAS when increased.
proposal.expected_effect: Increased per-basin training diversity should reduce peak-flow overfitting variance, improving median KGE and log-NSE while curbing PBIAS instability, without the capacity-driven PBIAS degradation seen when n_estimators/max_depth/max_samples were increased.

proposal.hypothesis: Among all single-factor RF mutations tried so far, the only one to nearly match the no-op baseline composite (56.62) was i12's removal of the 60-day window (56.55), showing that pruning redundant antecedent windows within the model's effective 90-day range costs little unlike every capacity-reducing (depth/leaf) or feature-addition mutation, which all scored notably worse (51-55); the 30-day window sits directly between the still-retained 14-day and 60-day windows and duplicates similar sub-seasonal soil-moisture/precipitation memory, so it is the next most redundant, genuinely untested window to prune.
proposal.expected_effect: Removing the redundant 30-day window should reduce split-quality dilution from collinear antecedent features, maintaining or slightly improving median KGE/log-NSE and PBIAS stability relative to baseline without the capacity or feature-addition penalties seen in prior rejected mutations.

proposal.hypothesis: RF's max_dynamic_window=90 makes only windows {1,3,7,14,30,60,90} effective, and removing either the 60-day (i12, composite 56.55) or 30-day (i14, composite 56.76) window individually matched or beat the no-op baseline (56.62) by reducing split dilution among adjacent redundant mid-range windows, so removing both together should compound that decorrelation benefit while retaining short-term (1-14d) and seasonal (90d) memory.
proposal.expected_effect: median_abs_pbias should improve further (below the 7.47-7.81 seen from single-window removals) driving a higher composite score, while median_kge and median_log_nse remain stable since core short- and long-range antecedent information is preserved.

proposal.hypothesis: The 90-day window is the longest antecedent window random_forest actually uses (max_dynamic_window=90 caps effective windows at {1,3,7,14,30,60,90}), so it overlaps most heavily with static soil/geology/climate attributes and, following the pattern where isolated removal of the adjacent 60-day (i12, composite 56.55) and 30-day (i14, composite 56.76) windows matched or beat the 56.62 no-op baseline while their joint removal (i15) hurt (56.53), removing the untested 90-day window alone should cut redundant split competition at the model's effective boundary without compounding the over-pruning seen in i15.
proposal.expected_effect: Composite score should match or exceed the 56.62 no-op baseline via reduced abs_pbias from less redundant long-window split dilution, while keeping median_kge closer to baseline than the 30-day-removal (i14) trade-off since the 60-day window remains intact for medium-term soil-moisture memory.

proposal.hypothesis: Only the decreasing direction of max_samples (0.75->0.6, i06) has been tested and it hurt KGE, so the untested increasing direction (0.75->0.9) should let each tree see a larger, more representative bootstrap sample-including more peak-flow events-reducing inter-tree sampling variance without touching depth or leaf-size capacity that drove the PBIAS degradations in i07/i08/i10.
proposal.expected_effect: Median KGE and log NSE should improve or hold steady as trees train on more complete bootstrap draws capturing rare peak flows, while PBIAS should improve or remain stable due to lower ensemble-level sampling variance, without the capacity-driven overfitting seen when depth/leaf/estimator counts were increased.

proposal.hypothesis: n_estimators is the only core random_forest hyperparameter never yet mutated in isolation, and unlike depth/leaf-size/bootstrap-fraction (which all control per-tree capacity and consistently worsened PBIAS when increased), adding more trees only increases ensemble averaging and should reduce prediction variance without raising per-tree overfitting risk.
proposal.expected_effect: median_kge and median_log_nse should improve modestly and median_abs_pbias should hold steady or improve slightly, since averaging over more trees dampens idiosyncratic per-basin peak-flow overfitting without increasing individual tree capacity.

proposal.hypothesis: surf_press is largely a proxy for elevation/climate normals already encoded in the static topography and climate feature families, so as a dynamic input it mainly adds low-signal split dimensions that dilute tree quality (mirroring how removing redundant mid-range rolling windows in i12/i14 matched or beat baseline), and no dynamic-feature removal has yet been tested in isolation.
proposal.expected_effect: median_abs_pbias should improve (lower) via reduced split dilution and less basin-specific overfitting to a low-information channel, while median_kge and median_log_nse should stay roughly stable since surf_press's unique hydrological signal is largely redundant with existing static topography/climate attributes.

proposal.hypothesis: Among all single-factor RF mutations tried, only enlarging the bootstrap sample fraction (max_samples 0.75->0.9) simultaneously improved KGE, log-NSE, and PBIAS over baseline, while every capacity lever (min_samples_leaf up, deeper trees implied, more per-basin samples) worsened PBIAS via basin-specific peak memorization, so pushing max_samples to its allowed ceiling should further reduce inter-tree sampling variance and peak-flow exposure gaps without adding tree capacity.
proposal.expected_effect: Median KGE and log-NSE should improve modestly and PBIAS should decrease further as each tree sees a fuller, more representative bootstrap sample (more peak events), continuing the trend observed when raising max_samples from 0.75 to 0.9, without the failure-rate or bias costs seen from capacity-increasing mutations.

proposal.hypothesis: All recent mutations perturbing subsample/colsample/reg_lambda/depth around the best config underperformed, suggesting the tree ensemble is already near a local optimum for coarse-step boosting; using a finer learning rate with proportionally more trees should reduce residual variance and improve KGE/log-NSE without changing model capacity.
proposal.expected_effect: Finer boosting steps should smooth the fitted response surface, modestly improving median KGE and log-NSE while keeping abs PBIAS and failure rate stable since the effective boosting budget (n_estimators*learning_rate) remains comparable to the current best.

proposal.hypothesis: Repeated tree-hyperparameter mutations (depth, subsample, colsample, reg_lambda, learning_rate) around the 74.2-score best have all underperformed, including a finer-learning-rate variant that collapsed to score 25.7, suggesting the shallow (depth=4) ensemble is data-starved rather than mis-tuned, so increasing the number of training samples drawn per basin should give the model more signal to fit basin-specific nonlinearities without altering model capacity.
proposal.expected_effect: More training rows per catchment should reduce residual variance and abs_pbias by letting the fixed-capacity trees better resolve basin-specific rating relationships, improving median_kge and median_log_nse over the 300-sample baseline.

proposal.hypothesis: Bootstrap fraction shows a monotonic trend within the tested range (0.6 worse, 0.75 baseline, 0.9 best so far in i17 with higher KGE/log-NSE and lower |PBIAS|), suggesting each tree benefits from seeing a larger, more representative in-bag sample with more peak-flow events, so pushing max_samples to the range ceiling of 1.0 tests whether this trend continues before any variance-reduction benefit saturates.
proposal.expected_effect: Median KGE and median log-NSE should improve further (or at least hold near i17's levels) and median |PBIAS| should stay reduced relative to the 0.75 baseline, continuing the gains from i17's 0.9 test without raising failure_rate.

proposal.hypothesis: Prior leaf/depth mutations only tested the capacity-restricting direction (larger min_samples_leaf / shallower depth) and consistently hurt performance, while the analogous capacity-loosening direction for bagging (raising max_samples toward 0.9) was the single best-performing lever found so far, so decreasing min_samples_leaf lets trees fit finer local nonlinearities (especially peak-flow recessions) that coarser leaves smooth away, with variance controlled by the existing 200-tree ensemble.
proposal.expected_effect: median_kge and median_log_nse should improve as trees resolve peak and low-flow transitions more precisely, with only a modest, ensemble-buffered increase in abs_pbias/failure_rate.

proposal.hypothesis: Bootstrap fraction shows a non-monotonic response with a peak at max_samples=0.9 (i17, composite 57.63, best of all tested mutations) that declined again at the range ceiling of 1.0 (i01, composite 52.30), so the true optimum likely lies between 0.9 and 1.0 rather than at either tested endpoint.
proposal.expected_effect: Narrowing the bootstrap fraction toward 0.95 should further reduce inter-tree variance versus the 0.9 baseline while avoiding the near-full-replication coverage loss seen at 1.0, nudging median_kge and composite score above the 57.63 achieved at 0.9 without degrading PBIAS.

proposal.hypothesis: max_samples shows a sharp non-monotonic peak in the tested range (0.6 worse, 0.75 baseline=53.64, 0.9=57.63 best, 0.95=53.64, 1.0=52.30 worst), so testing an intermediate value between the baseline and the observed peak should confirm whether the improvement rises smoothly toward 0.9 or whether 0.9 is a narrow local optimum, refining the location of the true optimum.
proposal.expected_effect: If the trend from baseline (0.75) to the peak (0.9) is smooth, KGE and composite score should improve monotonically toward the i17 level (~57.6) with reduced PBIAS, confirming a broad optimum region rather than a noisy spike at 0.9.

proposal.hypothesis: Every tested loosening of per-tree capacity has helped (max_samples 0.85->0.9 produced the best composite so far at 57.63; min_samples_leaf decrease in i02 beat baseline too), while max_depth=18 is the one core capacity parameter never yet mutated in isolation, so raising it toward the range ceiling should let individual trees resolve more nonlinear peak-flow structure.
proposal.expected_effect: median_kge and median_log_nse should rise as deeper trees capture finer nonlinear rainfall-runoff relationships, with only modest risk to median_abs_pbias/failure_rate since the increase (18->24) stays well below the range ceiling of 30.

proposal.hypothesis: sample_per_basin_train has never been mutated in isolation despite being an approved lever, and since RF's best-performing changes so far all involved giving trees more representative in-bag data (max_samples raised to 0.9 in i17 was the top scorer), increasing the number of training samples drawn per basin should similarly improve coverage of each catchment's flow regime, including rarer peak-flow states, without touching per-tree capacity parameters that repeatedly hurt PBIAS when loosened.
proposal.expected_effect: Denser per-basin sampling should improve median KGE and reduce median |PBIAS| by giving trees a more representative and complete picture of each catchment's discharge distribution, particularly for under-sampled peak-flow periods, while leaving failure_rate unaffected since no structural or capacity parameters change.

proposal.hypothesis: sample_per_basin_train=+increase (i06) was the only tested change that simultaneously improved KGE (0.621, best of all runs), log-NSE (0.669, best of all runs), PBIAS (6.82%, best of all runs) and halved the failure rate (0.01 vs 0.03 elsewhere), indicating denser per-basin sampling better captures each catchment's flow regime including rare high-flow events, so pushing sample_per_basin_train further toward the range ceiling should extend that broad-based skill gain rather than trading one metric off against another as every capacity-based lever (max_samples, min_samples_leaf, max_depth, n_estimators) has done.
